extracted.intended_audience: experimental natural philosophers / scientists (readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed experimental report of vacuum (exhausted receiver) trials on animals and liquids, describing apparatus, procedure, observations, and tentative interpretations. Aimed at documenting methods, results, anomalies, and suggestions for further enquiry so others can reproduce or extend the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed apparatus description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the structure and use of instruments and vessels used (receivers, pumps, chemical pipes, measuring tubes, custom glass with slender stem), including dimensions and specific features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete dimensions and construction details (e.g., 'a clear round glass, with a pipe or stem of about nine inches in length, the globular part ... about 3-1/2 inches in diameter'; 'the pipe was, within an inch of the top, melted ... drawn out ... as slender as a crow's quill'). Explain special features and why they were chosen (to observe decrement of water, to prevent overflow, to permit bubbles to break).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-by-step procedural detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the sequence of operations (how animals or liquids were placed, pumping out air, resting the pump, letting air in) so the procedure can be replicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include actions and timing of actions (e.g., 'pumping out the air, the numerous bubbles disclosed themselves ... the pump was suffered to rest a while ... the pump was plied again'). Note precautions (leave off pumping before overflow; mend cracks; secure against ingress of air).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise timing and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Report durations and timings of major events (when animals became discomposed, how long they survived under exhaustion, time-points of observations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use watches/clocks and give times (e.g., 'within less than two minutes', 'above 2-1/2 hours', 'at the end of the half hour', 'within one minute or a little more'). When measuring liquids or bubbles, give lengths/volumes observed (inches, parts of an inch, ounces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition and multiple trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct and report repeated experiments and replicate under varied conditions (different animals, ages, sizes, different receiver sizes, multiple runs of the same trial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show multiple examples (Exp. I, II, III etc.), report differing outcomes between repeats (e.g., same species showing different durations), and include attempted repeats to test anomalies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of controls and comparison to isolate causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include comparative conditions to distinguish causes (e.g., test whether effects are due to absence of air versus closeness of vessel by sealing receiver with air inside).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly design contrasts: keep an animal in a close sealed vessel with air to show closeness alone doesn't produce convulsions; compare water-fowl and hens; compare animals of different ages and constitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful observation of phenomena and fine detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Record qualitative observational details (swelling, foaming, color changes, transparency, gape of jaws, tongue position, foam sticking to glass, blistering, motions) with care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note small features that may bear on interpretation (e.g., 'the epiglottis ... was protruded', 'the mouth was grown blackish within', 'the body swelled', 'foam stuck to the inside of the glass').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report anomalies and negative or unexpected results honestly
rubrics_metrics.description: Include trials with differing or surprising outcomes and do not omit cases that contradict general trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State such outcomes and rationale for including them (e.g., 'I have purposely ... subjoined some trials, whose events are not altogether such as others would invite one to expect; but I purposely do it, not only to be true to the impartiality ...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for sources of variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and list factors that may cause variation in results (season, strength, bulk, age, peculiar constitutions of animals, size of receiver, instrument leaks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly call attention to these factors when interpreting outcomes and when designing further trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument design for sensitivity and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Design instruments to make small effects observable while protecting against hazards (prevent overflow, avoid glass breakage), and adapt geometry to magnify measurable changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for shapes and slender sections (e.g., slender pipe to make decrement of water visible; wider part to allow bubbles to break so water doesn't overflow). Note safety measures (stop pumping before danger of breaking glass).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative estimation even with uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempt to quantify elusive quantities (e.g., air latent in water) with the best available measurement and state the uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give numerical estimates and describe measurement procedure and limitations (e.g., 'the air collected ... was the first time 4-1/4 of an inch ... the second time we estimated it but 1/4 and 3/8'). Note when accuracy is limited and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive caution and posing of queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overconfident conclusions; state queries and suggest further experiments or theoretical questions arising from the observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pose explicit queries for future work (e.g., 'Query. Whether any considerable proportion of bubbles will be afforded by the same liquor ...?'; 'How far ... air latent in water ... of use to fishes?'). Recommend further systematic investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural care and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and clean apparatus and materials to avoid contamination or spoilage that would affect results (e.g., clean grease and scum in vinegar-making casks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report routine maintenance steps and frequencies (e.g., 'they take care to do clean away ... scum ... almost every year once'; 'clear away every morning ... the grease that is on the sides of the vessel').

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe limits of detection and measurement outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Report when an expected effect is not detectably present and note limits (e.g., water level change not perceptible beyond a hair's breadth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state null observations and consider instrumental resolution and experimental causes for non-detection ('I could not, by attentively comparing ... discern the difference to amount to above a hair's breadth').

rubrics_metrics.name: Document repair, sealing, and leak-handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Record how breaches or leaks were handled (mending with cloth dipped in cement, ensuring receiver is staunch) and their influence on results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note instances where cracks or leaks affected trials and corrective measures, and indicate whether these may have altered outcomes (e.g., sudden ingress of air bringing an imprisoned frog a reprieve).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of graded specimen selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Test across a range of specimen types and developmental stages to explore dependence on size/age (e.g., ducklings vs adult ducks, small vs large frogs, newly-kittened kittens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report selection criteria and compare outcomes across classes, and note recommendations for extending trials to other young animals to test hypotheses about durability under exhaustion.
